title: Body fluid spill and sharps clean-up (high-risk: trained workers only)
audience: Trained cleaning operative who may be called to a body fluid spill or a sharp on a job. This is a high-risk task. Work on it only after the training required by the employer.
learningOutcomes: Describe the protective steps before contact with a body fluid spill, including covering open cuts and selecting the spill kit and PPE.
Contain, absorb, disinfect and remove a body fluid spill in the order the procedure sets, allowing the disinfectant its full contact time.
Remove a sharp using a litter picker or grips and place it in a sharps container, never in general waste.
Dispose of soiled materials, PPE and equipment through the clinical waste route the site uses, and explain the decontamination of reusable tools.

instruction.heading: High-risk warning
instruction.body: Body fluids and sharps can carry blood-borne and other infectious agents. A needle stick or a splash to the eye or to broken skin is a serious incident. This lesson is written as a high-risk task. It is written to be complete, not reduced. Work on any body fluid spill or sharp only after the training your employer requires, with the spill kit and PPE provided, and with a supervisor or first-aid trained colleague aware of what you are doing. If the spill is large, the material is unknown, or you cannot carry out the steps safely, stop, protect the area and call for help. Completing this lesson does not qualify you to clean biohazard or crime-scene material, which is covered by separate high-risk lessons.

instruction.heading: Protecting yourself before you start
instruction.body: Check your hands for open cuts, grazes and broken skin. Cover any open wound with a waterproof dressing before you put on gloves. Put on the gloves and eye protection provided. Use the spill kit's protective clothing as the kit instructions require. Keep bystanders away, and rope off or barrier the area. Keep ventilation open where possible, because cleaning products give off fumes that should not be breathed. The equipment in the spill kit is single-use for the spill and should not be reused for other jobs.

instruction.heading: Clearing the sharps first
instruction.body: If there are sharps or needles in the spill, remove them before anything else. Use a litter picker or grips from the sharps container, not your hands. Place each sharp directly into an appropriate sharps container, and place the container on the floor while you put contaminated items into it, as the procedure directs. Never put a sharp into general waste, and never try to recap or bend a needle.

instruction.heading: Containing and absorbing the spill
instruction.body: Cover the liquid with the absorbent granules from the spill kit, or another approved absorbent. Work from the outside of the spill toward the centre so the spill does not spread. Scoop up as much of the contamination as possible with a scoop or scraper. Use absorbent paper towel to pick up the rest. Put every item used in the clean-up into the clinical waste bag as you go.

instruction.heading: Disinfecting and finishing the area
instruction.body: Spray the approved disinfectant over the area and leave the full contact time on the label, because the disinfectant needs that time to reduce the numbers of bacteria to a safe level. Mop or wipe the area and rinse it clean. Repeat the disinfect and wipe steps for any stubborn residue. Give the area a final rinse and let it dry. Check that no residue remains before the area is released for use.

instruction.heading: Disposal and decontamination
instruction.body: Put all soiled materials and used PPE into the clinical waste bag and seal the bag. The source procedure states that contaminated items are sent for incineration. Litter pickers, scoops and other reusable tools must be disinfected before they are used again. Wash your hands thoroughly after removing gloves, and put a fresh waterproof dressing on any plaster or wound that has been exposed. Keep colour coding for cloths and buckets so clean and contaminated items never mix.

instruction.heading: What the finished job looks like
instruction.body: The area should look clean and dry, be free of visible residue, and smell neutral once the disinfectant has been allowed to work. The customer should not be exposed to harmful bacteria or to needles. All waste is sealed and removed through the designated route. The sharps container is closed and stored in its locked area. The incident is recorded and reported, even when no one was hurt.

procedure: Stop and assess the spill. If it is large, unknown, or beyond your training, protect the area and call for help.
Check hands for cuts or broken skin, and cover any wound with a waterproof dressing before putting on gloves.
Put on the gloves, eye protection and protective clothing from the spill kit.
Barrier the area, keep bystanders away, and open ventilation where possible.
Remove any sharps with a litter picker or grips and place them into the sharps container.
Cover the liquid with absorbent and work from the outside toward the centre.
Scoop up the contamination, pick up the rest with absorbent paper, and bag everything used.
Spray disinfectant over the area and allow the full contact time on the label.
Mop or wipe the area clean and rinse. Repeat if residue remains.
Give the area a final rinse and dry, then check that no residue remains.
Seal the clinical waste bag and dispose of it through the site's route.
Disinfect reusable tools, remove PPE, wash your hands thoroughly, and renew any dressing.
Record the job, the materials used, the sharps count, and any incident or exposure, and report it immediately.

workedExamples.situation: A worker is called to clean a blood spill near a toilet in a shared office. A sharp is lying in the spill, and the worker has a small cut on one thumb.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: In what order does the worker act, and what do they do about the cut?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker covers the cut with a waterproof dressing before putting on gloves, so the wound is not exposed to the spill. The sharp is removed first with a litter picker or grips into the sharps container. Then the spill is absorbed, disinfected for its full contact time, wiped, rinsed, and bagged. If the worker is not trained for this task, they stop and call a trained colleague rather than attempting the clean.

workedExamples.situation: A worker has finished a spill clean-up and places a used litter picker back in the storage cupboard without disinfecting it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the worker do, and why does it matter?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker should disinfect the litter picker before it is used again. Reusable tools that touched body fluid can carry contamination to the next job. The worker should report the storage step to the supervisor so the tool is checked, and then follow the disinfect step for every reusable tool after a spill.

equipmentAndPpe: Bodily fluids spill kit with absorbent granules, scoop and scraper, and protective clothing
Disposable gloves and eye protection, as provided
Litter pickers or grips for sharps
Rigid sharps container, kept in a locked storage area
Clinical waste bags, sealed before removal
Waterproof dressings for any cut or broken skin

commonErrors.error: Touching a sharp with the hands, or bending or recapping it.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a litter picker or grips only, and place the sharp straight into the rigid sharps container.

commonErrors.error: Putting on gloves over an open cut.
commonErrors.prevention: Cover every open wound with a waterproof dressing before gloves go on.

commonErrors.error: Wiping the disinfectant away before its contact time has passed.
commonErrors.prevention: Time the contact period from the label and keep the area closed until it has passed.

commonErrors.error: Placing sharps or contaminated items in general waste.
commonErrors.prevention: Sharps go into rigid containers only. Contaminated items go into clinical waste bags only.

commonErrors.error: Storing reusable tools without disinfecting them.
commonErrors.prevention: Disinfect litter pickers, scoops and other reusable tools after every spill, before they go back into storage.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: High-risk task. Work on body fluid spills and sharps only after the training required by the employer. Completing this lesson does not certify you to clean these materials, and the lesson does not grant any licence or authority.
Clinical waste handling, including incineration, must follow the site's clinical waste route and the rules of the relevant state or territory.
Disinfectants and cleaning chemicals must be used as the label directs, with the safety data sheet available on site.

Any needle stick, splash to the eye or broken skin must be reported immediately and first aid started. Follow the site's incident and exposure procedure. Post-exposure medical advice is outside this lesson.

Stop work and call for help if the spill is large, the material is unidentified, or you cannot carry out the steps safely. Biohazard and crime-scene material is outside this lesson and needs the separate high-risk lessons.

qualityStandard: No sharp is left in the work area, and every sharp is in a rigid container.
No contaminated material is in general waste, and all clinical waste bags are sealed.
Disinfectant was left for its full label contact time before the area was wiped.
The area is clean, dry and free of visible residue, and it is released only after a check.
All reusable tools were disinfected before they went back into storage.
documentationEvidence: Incident or spill report, with time, location and materials involved
Number of sharps found and removed, and the container used
Disinfectant product and label reference, with contact time
Clinical waste bags used and the disposal route
Record of any cut, exposure or first aid given, and the person notified
summary: Stop and assess first. Work on this task only after the training your employer requires.
Cover open cuts with a waterproof dressing, then put on gloves and eye protection, before you touch the spill.
Remove sharps first with a litter picker or grips into a rigid container, never into general waste.
Absorb, disinfect for the full contact time, rinse, dry, bag all waste, and disinfect reusable tools before storage.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker has a small cut on one hand and must clean a body fluid spill. What should happen before gloves go on?
options: Put the gloves on over the cut and carry on with the spill
Cover the cut with a waterproof dressing, then put on the gloves
Wash the cut and continue without covering it and then carry on
Ask the customer to clean the spill instead while you wait outside

knowledgeChecks.question: Once the spill has been cleaned, where do the used absorbent materials, PPE and contaminated cloths go?
options: A clinical waste bag, which is sealed before removal
The general waste bin, once the lid is closed for the day
Down a drain, flushed with a large volume of water

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about sharps is correct?
options: Sharps may go into general waste once they are wrapped in paper
Sharps must never go into general waste and must go into an appropriate container
Sharps should be picked up by hand and carried in a pocket to the bin
Sharps need a container only if they are visibly bloodstained
